answer: Attention Ledger with Decay. Each identity must hold a kernel of verified interaction history: a rolling record of responses to unpredictable prompts, scored by latency and consistency. Scores decay unless refreshed, so idle clones lose standing. New identities start on a narrow ledge with capped visibility and must climb through sustained real-time participation. The dune of accumulated score erodes without continuous work. An attacker pays the opportunity cost of running many identities through live, timed tasks simultaneously, which caps how many can stay credible at once.
